cleanIntro: Two things about this book have to be settled before a single screw is turned. First, it carves the LE SERIES out of its own coverage — its title reads "Models 10/110 (excluding ‘LE SERIES’)", so an LE Series 110 is a different rifle in a different manual and nothing below is sourced for it. Second, Savage builds the 110 in two incompatible layouts — SIDE BOLT RELEASE and BOTTOM BOLT RELEASE — and puts identifying which one you own squarely on the owner: Section 3 is the bottom release, Section 4 is the side release, and everything else in the book is common. They differ in how the bolt comes out and in how the stock comes off, so following the wrong one gets you a bolt that will not release and a rear action screw you cannot find. The field strip itself is the bolt out and the barrelled action out of the stock. Past that Savage stops you at the bolt assembly, which is serial-matched to the receiver and is not to be taken apart.

steps.title: An 'LE SERIES' 110 is not this book
steps.action: Look at your rifle before you look at this guide. Savage's own title for this manual excludes the LE SERIES of the 10/110 by name, so if what you own is an LE Series rifle then the procedures below are not the ones Savage published for it — the LE and Varmint/Target rifles are covered in a separate book. A plain 110 out of general production is what this manual covers, along with the 11/111, 14/114 and 16/116. If you cannot tell from the rollmark or the paperwork which you have, treat that as unresolved and get the right manual rather than assuming.
steps.prose: This is a coverage bound the manufacturer set, not a caution we added: the exclusion is printed in the manual's own title.
steps.quote: Models 10/110 (excluding 'LE SERIES'), 11/111, 14/114 and 16/116 Bolt Action Centerfire Rifles
steps.cite: Models 10/110 (excluding ‘LE SERIES’), 11/111, 14/114 and 16/116 Bolt Action Centerfire Rifles — REV. 3 (08/19) — printed on the manual's own back page as "108831 REV. 3 (08/19)" — Cover / title, p.1
steps.warn: This manual excludes the 10/110 LE SERIES. An LE Series rifle needs its own book.

steps.title: SIDE BOLT RELEASE or BOTTOM BOLT RELEASE — you have to decide which you own
steps.action: Find the bolt release before anything else, because on the 110 there are two designs and they are not variations of one procedure. A BOTTOM BOLT RELEASE rifle has a button that pushes into the trigger guard, and its rear action screw hides underneath it. A SIDE BOLT RELEASE rifle uses the cocking indicator on the flat of the receiver as the release, pressed downward. Savage puts the identification on the owner in plain words and then splits the book: Section 3 is the bottom release, Section 4 is the side release. Work out which is in your hands now — mistaking one for the other will have you pressing at empty air while the bolt refuses to leave the receiver.
steps.prose: The stock removal differs too, not just the bolt. Neither section is a safe stand-in for the other.
steps.caution: Identify your bolt release type first. Section 3 = bottom, Section 4 = side.
steps.quote: Savage Arms offers firearms designed in two ways: SIDE BOLT RELEASE and BOTTOM BOLT RELEASE. It is important to identify which firearm you have purchased and follow the appropriate section in the INSTRUCTION MANUAL.
steps.cite: Models 10/110 (excluding ‘LE SERIES’), 11/111, 14/114 and 16/116 Bolt Action Centerfire Rifles — REV. 3 (08/19) — printed on the manual's own back page as "108831 REV. 3 (08/19)" — Introduction, p.1

steps.title: The 110 safety is THREE position, and full safe locks the bolt shut
steps.action: Understand this safety before you unload, because it behaves differently from the two-position Savages. In FULL SAFE the trigger is blocked and the bolt cannot be opened at all. The MID position is the one that lets you cycle the action with the trigger still blocked, and you reach it by a specific sequence: lift the bolt handle, move the safety to FULL SAFE, then push the bolt handle back down. That is how a loaded 110 is unloaded without ever taking the safety off.
steps.caution: FULL SAFE locks the bolt closed. MID SAFE is the unloading position.
steps.quote: MID SAFE POSITION MID POSITION ALLOWS THE BOLT TO BE OPENED AND CYCLED WHILE STILL BLOCKING THE TRIGGER
steps.cite: Models 10/110 (excluding ‘LE SERIES’), 11/111, 14/114 and 16/116 Bolt Action Centerfire Rifles — REV. 3 (08/19) — printed on the manual's own back page as "108831 REV. 3 (08/19)" — Section 2, Three Position Safety, p.6

steps.title: Unload with a hand over the ejection port
steps.action: With the safety in MID SAFE, put one hand over the ejection port, keep your finger completely away from the trigger and outside the guard, then lift the bolt handle and draw it slowly rearward to extract the chambered cartridge into your hand. Slowly is the operative word on a 110 — the ejector is spring-loaded and a brisk pull throws the round across the room rather than into your palm. On a top-loading rifle, push the bolt fully forward again to pick up the next cartridge behind the extractor and repeat until the magazine is empty. A detachable-box rifle simply gives up its magazine first; a hinged floor plate drops its cartridges into your hand when the release is pushed.
steps.quote: Placing one hand over the ejection port, your finger completely away from the trigger and out of the trigger guard, lift the bolt handle and slowly pull to the rear to extract the cartridge from the chamber.
steps.cite: Models 10/110 (excluding ‘LE SERIES’), 11/111, 14/114 and 16/116 Bolt Action Centerfire Rifles — REV. 3 (08/19) — printed on the manual's own back page as "108831 REV. 3 (08/19)" — Section 5, Unloading Your Rifle, p.17

steps.title: Look and feel — chamber and magazine both
steps.action: Once the last round is out, look into the chamber and into the magazine well and then check both with a finger. On a 110 the magazine can be a detachable box, an internal top-load with a follower, or a hinged floor plate, and each hides a round in a different place — the top-load in particular holds cartridges under the follower where a glance across the receiver will not see them. Savage's instruction is not to assume. Do the check with the rifle pointed somewhere safe and the bolt back.
steps.quote: LOOK AND FEEL! BE SURE THE CHAMBER AND MAGAZINE ARE COMPLETELY EMPTY -DO NOT ASSUME!
steps.cite: Models 10/110 (excluding ‘LE SERIES’), 11/111, 14/114 and 16/116 Bolt Action Centerfire Rifles — REV. 3 (08/19) — printed on the manual's own back page as "108831 REV. 3 (08/19)" — Section 5, Unloading Your Rifle, p.17
steps.warn: Chamber AND magazine, by eye and by finger.

steps.title: BOTTOM BOLT RELEASE — trigger back first, then the release into the guard
steps.action: This is the Section 3 procedure and it applies only if your rifle's release is the button in the trigger guard. With the muzzle safe, move the safety forward to SAFETY OFF — READY TO FIRE, lift the bolt handle and pull it fully to the rear, then with no ammunition in the rifle pull the trigger fully rearward and hold it there. Now push the bolt release as far as it will go into the trigger guard. Both hands are committed at that point, which is why the rifle wants to be resting on the bench rather than held up.
steps.prose: Note the safety has to come OFF for this. Prove the rifle empty before that happens, not after.
steps.quote: move the safety forward to the SAFETY OFF - READY TO FIRE position. 2. Lift the bolt handle and pull fully to the rear. 3. WITH NO AMMUNITION IN THE FIREARM, pull the TRIGGER (1) fully rearward and hold it in that position.
steps.cite: Models 10/110 (excluding ‘LE SERIES’), 11/111, 14/114 and 16/116 Bolt Action Centerfire Rifles — REV. 3 (08/19) — printed on the manual's own back page as "108831 REV. 3 (08/19)" — Section 3, Bolt Removal — Bottom Bolt Release, p.7
steps.warn: The trigger is pulled during this. The rifle must already be proved empty.

steps.title: BOTTOM BOLT RELEASE — draw the bolt out clear of the stock
steps.action: Holding the trigger and the release, take the bolt handle and pull the bolt assembly fully rearward until it clears the receiver, watching that the handle does not swing down into the comb of the stock on its way out. If it binds or stops part way, that is not a tight bolt — it is the sear or the bolt stop still in the way, and Savage names the order: trigger fully rearward first, then the bolt release pushed as far as it will go into the trigger guard. Release both, start over, and it comes out cleanly.
steps.quote: If it seems to bind or stop, be sure that the trigger has been pulled fully rearward first and then the BOLT RELEASE pushed as far as it will go into the trigger guard.
steps.cite: Models 10/110 (excluding ‘LE SERIES’), 11/111, 14/114 and 16/116 Bolt Action Centerfire Rifles — REV. 3 (08/19) — printed on the manual's own back page as "108831 REV. 3 (08/19)" — Section 3, Bolt Removal — Bottom Bolt Release, p.7

steps.title: SIDE BOLT RELEASE — the cocking indicator IS the release
steps.action: This is the Section 4 procedure, and it applies only if your rifle has no button in the trigger guard. On a side-release 110 the part you press is the cocking indicator on the flat of the receiver — Savage also calls it the side bolt release — and it goes down, not in. Safety forward to READY TO FIRE, bolt handle lifted and pulled fully back, trigger held fully rearward with no ammunition present, then press the cocking indicator as far down as it will go and draw the bolt out, keeping the handle clear of the stock. If it binds, the same two things are the cause: the trigger was not fully back, or the indicator was not pressed all the way down.
steps.prose: That is the same part that tells you whether the rifle is cocked, which is why it sits proud of the receiver flat.
steps.caution: Side-release rifles only. There is no button in the trigger guard to press.
steps.quote: move the safety forward to the SAFETY OFF - READY TO FIRE position. 2. Lift the bolt handle and pull fully to the rear. 3. WITH NO AMMUNITION IN THE FIREARM, pull the TRIGGER (1) fully rearward and hold it in that position. 4. Push the COCKING INDICATOR (2) - also known as the "SIDE BOLT RELEASE" as far down as it will go. 5. Grasping the BOLT HANDLE, pull the bolt assembly fully rearward until it clears the receiver, being careful not to hit the stock.
steps.cite: Models 10/110 (excluding ‘LE SERIES’), 11/111, 14/114 and 16/116 Bolt Action Centerfire Rifles — REV. 3 (08/19) — printed on the manual's own back page as "108831 REV. 3 (08/19)" — Section 4, Bolt Removal — Side Bolt Release, p.11

steps.title: Read the four digits by the extractor before this bolt goes back
steps.action: With the bolt in your hand, find the four digits engraved beside the extractor and check them against the last four of the serial number on the receiver. On a Savage 110 that engraving records that this bolt head was fitted to this barrel, so it is the one check that has to happen before installation and not after. Read it now, while the bolt is out and the receiver is in front of you. If the two do not match, that bolt does not belong in that rifle and it must not be fitted.
steps.quote: BEFORE INSTALLING THE BOLT, VERIFY THAT THE 4 DIGITS ENGRAVED BY THE EXTRACTOR MATCH THE LAST 4 DIGITS OF THE SERIAL NUMBER ON THE RECEIVER.
steps.cite: Models 10/110 (excluding ‘LE SERIES’), 11/111, 14/114 and 16/116 Bolt Action Centerfire Rifles — REV. 3 (08/19) — printed on the manual's own back page as "108831 REV. 3 (08/19)" — Section 3, Installing and Removing the Bolt Assembly, p.6
steps.warn: Four digits by the extractor = last four of the receiver serial number.

steps.title: A 110 bolt fits one 110 and no other
steps.action: Never put another Savage bolt in this receiver, even one from an identical model in the same chambering. Savage says bolt assemblies are specifically matched to a firearm and names the outcome — extensive damage to the rifle, serious injury to the shooter or bystanders. The reason is headspace: this design sets the bolt-face-to-shoulder distance through the fitted bolt head, so a foreign bolt sets it wrong in one direction or the other, and neither direction is survivable in a centrefire cartridge. Keep the bolt with its own rifle from the moment it comes out.
steps.quote: BOLT ASSEMBLIES ARE SPECIFICALLY MATCHED TO A FIREARM. USING ANY OTHER BOLT ASSEMBLY MAY CAUSE EXTENSIVE DAMAGE TO THE FIREARM AND/OR SERIOUS INJURY TO THE SHOOTER OR BYSTANDER.
steps.cite: Models 10/110 (excluding ‘LE SERIES’), 11/111, 14/114 and 16/116 Bolt Action Centerfire Rifles — REV. 3 (08/19) — printed on the manual's own back page as "108831 REV. 3 (08/19)" — Section 11, Cleaning and Care of Your Firearm, p.33
steps.warn: One bolt, one rifle. Never interchange.

steps.title: BOTTOM BOLT RELEASE stock removal — the action stays closed and fired
steps.action: On a bottom-release rifle Savage has you dry fire before the stock comes off, and then keeps the rifle in that state throughout: bolt closed, action uncocked, for the whole of removing the stock and reinstalling the action. Check the chamber and magazine are empty again, remove the detachable box magazine or open the hinged floor plate, then with the muzzle pointed safely close the bolt and pull the trigger. Do not lift the bolt handle again until the rifle is back together — a cocked action jams the bolt release button as the action goes back into the stock, and Savage prints a whole recovery routine for that failure.
steps.prose: That recovery routine is: take the screws out, take the action out, cock it, dry fire it, and put it back. Avoiding it is easier.
steps.caution: Bottom-release rifles: bolt closed and action fired from here until reassembly is complete.
steps.quote: THE BOLT MUST REMAIN CLOSED AND THE ACTION UNCOCKED ('FIRED') THROUGHOUT THE ENTIRE PROCEDURE OF REMOVING THE STOCK AND THEN REINSTALLING THE ACTION.
steps.cite: Models 10/110 (excluding ‘LE SERIES’), 11/111, 14/114 and 16/116 Bolt Action Centerfire Rifles — REV. 3 (08/19) — printed on the manual's own back page as "108831 REV. 3 (08/19)" — Section 3, Removing the Stock, p.8

steps.title: BOTTOM BOLT RELEASE — the rear action screw lives under the bolt release
steps.action: Turn the rifle upside down with the muzzle away from you and push the bolt release as far as it will go into the trigger guard; that is what uncovers the rear action screw underneath it. Back that screw off with a 5/32-inch Allen wrench, then loosen the front screw — ahead of the magazine latch on a detachable-box rifle, or accessible under the plate on a hinged floor plate rifle. Remove both screws and lift the stock away. If you cannot see a rear screw at all with the release pressed, you are on a side-release rifle and reading the wrong section.
steps.quote: 5. Push the BOLT RELEASE as far as it will go into the trigger guard to gain access to the rear action screw, located under the BOLT RELEASE (see FIGURE 10).
steps.cite: Models 10/110 (excluding ‘LE SERIES’), 11/111, 14/114 and 16/116 Bolt Action Centerfire Rifles — REV. 3 (08/19) — printed on the manual's own back page as "108831 REV. 3 (08/19)" — Section 3, Removing the Stock, p.8

steps.title: SIDE BOLT RELEASE — two screws, 5/32-inch Allen, and that is all
steps.action: On a side-release rifle the stock comes off more simply: check the chamber and magazine are empty, turn the rifle upside down with the muzzle away from you, and loosen and remove the two screws securing the stock with a 5/32-inch Allen wrench. On a top-load rifle that is the whole job; on a detachable-box or hinged-floor-plate rifle you take the magazine out or open the plate first, and the front screw sits ahead of the magazine latch or under the plate. Support the barrelled action as the second screw comes out.
steps.prose: There is no dry-fire requirement in the side-release stock procedure — that instruction belongs to the bottom-release section.
steps.caution: 5/32" Allen. Do not substitute an undersized key.
steps.quote: Using a 5/32" Allen wrench, loosen and remove the two screws securing the stock (see FIGURE 18).
steps.cite: Models 10/110 (excluding ‘LE SERIES’), 11/111, 14/114 and 16/116 Bolt Action Centerfire Rifles — REV. 3 (08/19) — printed on the manual's own back page as "108831 REV. 3 (08/19)" — Section 4, Removing the Stock — Top Load (Internal Magazine), p.12

steps.title: Leave the small screw at the rear of the trigger guard alone
steps.action: There is a third screw at the rear of the trigger guard and it is not an action screw. Savage states it is there merely to hold the trigger guard in place, and that over-tightening it will damage the stock — on a 110 it bears directly into the wood or the polymer behind the guard, with no metal pillar under it. Do not remove it as part of a strip, and do not try to snug it up when everything else is being torqued. The two action screws are what hold the barrelled action to the stock.
steps.quote: DO NOT TIGHTEN THE SCREW AT THE REAR OF THE TRIGGER GUARD. INTENDED MERELY TO HOLD THE TRIGGER GUARD IN PLACE, OVER TIGHTENING THIS SCREW WILL CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE STOCK.
steps.cite: Models 10/110 (excluding ‘LE SERIES’), 11/111, 14/114 and 16/116 Bolt Action Centerfire Rifles — REV. 3 (08/19) — printed on the manual's own back page as "108831 REV. 3 (08/19)" — Section 3, Installing the Stock, p.9
steps.warn: Rear trigger guard screw: not an action screw. Do not tighten it.

steps.title: Never clean a loaded rifle, and only one rifle on the bench
steps.action: Confirm the chamber and magazine are empty once more before solvent appears, and keep this to one rifle at a time. Savage prints both instructions together at the head of the cleaning section for a reason that this model makes concrete: 110 bolts are serial-matched, they look identical across models and chamberings, and two rifles stripped side by side is precisely how two bolts change places. If a second rifle is waiting its turn, it waits with its own bolt in it.
steps.quote: DISASSEMBLE ONLY ONE FIREARM AT A TIME TO AVOID INTERCHANGING COMPONENTS.
steps.cite: Models 10/110 (excluding ‘LE SERIES’), 11/111, 14/114 and 16/116 Bolt Action Centerfire Rifles — REV. 3 (08/19) — printed on the manual's own back page as "108831 REV. 3 (08/19)" — Section 11, Cleaning and Care of Your Firearm, p.33
steps.warn: One firearm at a time. Never disassemble, clean or oil a loaded firearm.

steps.title: Solvent on the brush, and the rod goes in at the chamber
steps.action: Lay the rifle horizontally with the ejection port facing down, then run the correct-calibre rod in from the chamber end and out at the muzzle with a small amount of powder solvent on the brush, several passes. Port down is deliberate — it drops the loosened fouling and the solvent out of the receiver rather than letting it run back into the trigger inletting. Swap the brush for a patch tip and push clean patches through, again from the chamber, until they come out clean, then one oiled patch and one dry one behind it. With the bolt out there is no reason ever to rod a 110 from the muzzle and risk the crown.
steps.caution: Chamber end to muzzle, ejection port facing down.
steps.quote: Using a small amount of powder solvent on the brush, push the cleaning rod through the barrel several times.
steps.cite: Models 10/110 (excluding ‘LE SERIES’), 11/111, 14/114 and 16/116 Bolt Action Centerfire Rifles — REV. 3 (08/19) — printed on the manual's own back page as "108831 REV. 3 (08/19)" — Section 11, Cleaning and Care of Your Firearm, p.33

steps.title: The 110 bolt does not come apart
steps.action: Clean the bolt as a single unit — wipe the body, work solvent around the bolt head, extractor and ejector, dry it — and go no further. Savage bars the teardown outright, and the parts list shows what is waiting behind that instruction: an ejector, ejector spring and ejector retaining pin, a rear baffle assembly and a bolt assembly screw holding a compressed mainspring. Take that screw out on a bench and the spring stack leaves under its own power, and there is no published order for putting it back. Inspect the bolt head, extractor and ejector for wear while it is out, and leave them fitted.
steps.quote: DO NOT DISASSEMBLE THE BOLT ASSEMBLY.
steps.cite: Models 10/110 (excluding ‘LE SERIES’), 11/111, 14/114 and 16/116 Bolt Action Centerfire Rifles — REV. 3 (08/19) — printed on the manual's own back page as "108831 REV. 3 (08/19)" — Section 11, Protecting Metal Surfaces, p.33
steps.warn: Bolt exterior only. There is no published 110 bolt teardown.

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: In front of you should be the barrelled action, the stock, the two action screws, the bolt, and whichever magazine your rifle uses. That is the whole of what Savage publishes as owner disassembly for a non-LE 110. Use the access while you have it and do the inspection the manual asks for: bolt out, look down a clear barrel for obstructions, nicks, scratches, rust or pitting, and run your fingers down the outside of the barrel feeling for bulges. Deep Clean covers the AccuTrigger adjustment, the muzzle brake if yours has one, the interior metal surfaces, and getting the action back into the stock in the right order.
steps.prose: Remember which section you followed. The reassembly differs between the bottom-release and side-release rifles exactly as the strip did.
steps.quote: Remove the bolt, look down the barrel to be sure it is clear of any obstruction and that there are no signs of damage (nicks, scratches, etc.), rust, or pitting.
steps.cite: Models 10/110 (excluding ‘LE SERIES’), 11/111, 14/114 and 16/116 Bolt Action Centerfire Rifles — REV. 3 (08/19) — printed on the manual's own back page as "108831 REV. 3 (08/19)" — Section 11, Routine Maintenance, p.32

deepSteps.title: AccuTrigger adjustment on the 110 requires the stock off
deepSteps.action: If your 110 carries an AccuTrigger and you intend to adjust it, the stock has to come off first — Savage ties the two together in one instruction, unlike the Axis book where the guard alone comes down. Make sure the rifle is unloaded and the bolt is open before the stock is removed, and do the adjustment with the barrelled action out on the bench where you can see the trigger return spring from underneath. This is a deliberate job on a proved-empty rifle, not something folded into a cleaning session.
deepSteps.caution: Stock off before the AccuTrigger is touched on a 110.
deepSteps.quote: MAKE SURE THE FIREARM IS UNLOADED AND THE BOLT IS OPEN BEFORE REMOVING THE STOCK AND ADJUSTING THE ACCUTRIGGER.
deepSteps.cite: Models 10/110 (excluding ‘LE SERIES’), 11/111, 14/114 and 16/116 Bolt Action Centerfire Rifles — REV. 3 (08/19) — printed on the manual's own back page as "108831 REV. 3 (08/19)" — Section 6, AccuTrigger Adjustment, p.18

deepSteps.title: Clockwise for a heavier pull — the click is the ceiling
deepSteps.action: Insert the supplied AccuTrigger tool into the bottom of the trigger return spring so the slot engages the spring tail, then turn it clockwise to move toward the higher range of pull. The top of the range announces itself: the spring clicks as it rotates, and that click is the maximum, not a step on the way to more. Stop there. The tool turns the spring itself, so a screwdriver in its place slips off the tail and bends it.
deepSteps.quote: To adjust towards the higher range of pull, turn the tool clockwise. The maximum trigger pull is at the point where the spring "clicks" when rotated (see FIGURE 32).
deepSteps.cite: Models 10/110 (excluding ‘LE SERIES’), 11/111, 14/114 and 16/116 Bolt Action Centerfire Rifles — REV. 3 (08/19) — printed on the manual's own back page as "108831 REV. 3 (08/19)" — Section 6, AccuTrigger Adjustment, p.18

deepSteps.title: Counter-clockwise for a lighter pull — resistance is the floor
deepSteps.action: Turning the tool counter-clockwise takes the pull down, and the bottom of the range is defined mechanically rather than by a number: the large coil comes into contact with the top surface of the trigger and you feel resistance. That is the minimum. Savage is explicit that the spring is not to be forced past either limit, and forcing it past the low end is how a spring ends up unhooked with the trigger left without a return. Adjust in small increments and function-check between them with the stock back on.
deepSteps.quote: THE SPRING SHOULD NOT BE FORCED BEYOND THESE LIMITS.
deepSteps.cite: Models 10/110 (excluding ‘LE SERIES’), 11/111, 14/114 and 16/116 Bolt Action Centerfire Rifles — REV. 3 (08/19) — printed on the manual's own back page as "108831 REV. 3 (08/19)" — Section 6, AccuTrigger Adjustment, p.18
deepSteps.warn: Never force the spring past the click or past first resistance.

deepSteps.title: If your 110 has a muzzle brake, it is cleaned with an oil-free solvent
deepSteps.action: This applies only to rifles fitted with a Savage muzzle brake, adjustable or fixed. On the adjustable brake, put it in the closed position after use, apply a cleaning solvent that contains no oil — Savage's own example is a brake cleaner from an auto parts store — and then open and close the brake to work the solvent through the mechanism and flush the residue out. The whole point is what you must not do: oil in an adjustable brake increases carbon build-up and can make the brake malfunction. Bolt open and no ammunition in the chamber or magazine before you start, and never adjust a brake on a loaded rifle.
deepSteps.prose: A fixed brake is permanently open and has no open/closed cycle to work solvent through.
deepSteps.caution: No oil in an adjustable muzzle brake — it increases carbon build-up.
deepSteps.quote: Liberally apply a cleaning solvent that DOES NOT contain oil (such as a brake cleaner found in auto parts store).
deepSteps.cite: Models 10/110 (excluding ‘LE SERIES’), 11/111, 14/114 and 16/116 Bolt Action Centerfire Rifles — REV. 3 (08/19) — printed on the manual's own back page as "108831 REV. 3 (08/19)" — Section 7, To Clean the Adjustable Muzzle Brake, p.20

deepSteps.title: Leave the magazine assembly in the stock
deepSteps.action: On a top-load 110 the magazine box, follower assembly and retaining clip sit in the stock, and Savage states there is no reason to take that assembly out. The specific damage it warns about is deformation: pulling on the feeding lips or the sides distorts the box, and a distorted box gives you rounds that will not load or will not feed. Clean around it in place. If the parts do fall out of the stock on their own, the retaining clip goes into the side slot of the magazine, the plastic follower goes into the magazine, and the whole assembly pushes back into the stock as one.
deepSteps.quote: THERE IS NO REASON TO REMOVE THE MAGAZINE ASSEMBLY FROM THE STOCK. PULLING ON THE 'FEEDING LIPS' OR SIDES OF THE MAGAZINE MAY DISTORT ITS OVERALL SHAPE AND RESULT IN AMMUNITION NOT LOADING OR FEEDING RELIABLY.
deepSteps.cite: Models 10/110 (excluding ‘LE SERIES’), 11/111, 14/114 and 16/116 Bolt Action Centerfire Rifles — REV. 3 (08/19) — printed on the manual's own back page as "108831 REV. 3 (08/19)" — Section 4, Removing the Stock, p.11
deepSteps.warn: Never pull on the magazine's feeding lips or sides.

deepSteps.title: Interior metal, thin oil, and the bolt already out
deepSteps.action: With the bolt out and the stock off, the bolt raceways, the underside of the action and the recoil lug seat are reachable for the only time in this procedure. Take mud, twigs and grass off with a soft cloth first, then apply a thin coat of gun oil to the cleaned metal, rubbing where there are signs of rust. Where you can reach interior metal, clean and lightly oil it. Keep it to a very thin film — the trigger group sits in an open inletting directly under the action, and oil that runs off the receiver collects there with powder residue.
deepSteps.quote: Apply a thin coat of gun oil on all cleaned metal surfaces. Rubbing may be necessary to remove any signs of rust.
deepSteps.cite: Models 10/110 (excluding ‘LE SERIES’), 11/111, 14/114 and 16/116 Bolt Action Centerfire Rifles — REV. 3 (08/19) — printed on the manual's own back page as "108831 REV. 3 (08/19)" — Section 11, Protecting Metal Surfaces, p.33

deepSteps.title: Action screws start loose, then front first with the barrel pointing up
deepSteps.action: Put the action into the stock aligning the trigger with the trigger slot, then start both action screws — longer to the rear, shorter to the front — and turn them only until the threads just engage the receiver. The stock is deliberately loose at that point. Then stand the rifle up on its recoil pad with the barrel pointing skyward and press down on the barrel: that is what seats the recoil lug firmly into the stock before anything is torqued. Tighten the front screw first, then the rear, securely.
deepSteps.prose: Running one screw down tight before the other is engaged pulls the action out of square and leaves the lug half-seated.
deepSteps.caution: Both screws finger-loose first. Front screw first, rear second.
deepSteps.quote: Putting downward pressure on the barrel to seat the recoil lug firmly in the stock, tighten the front action screw first and then the rear action screw securely.
deepSteps.cite: Models 10/110 (excluding ‘LE SERIES’), 11/111, 14/114 and 16/116 Bolt Action Centerfire Rifles — REV. 3 (08/19) — printed on the manual's own back page as "108831 REV. 3 (08/19)" — Section 3, Installing the Stock, p.9

deepSteps.title: Cycle the bolt — a handle that will not close means the screws are swapped
deepSteps.action: With the stock back on, cycle the bolt several times and watch what the handle does. If it will not close fully, the action screws are in the wrong holes: the longer screw belongs at the rear, and the shorter one at the front, and putting the long screw in the front hole leaves its tip standing proud into the raceway. That is a mechanical check, not a feel — the bolt physically cannot close over the intruding screw. Swap them and cycle again.
deepSteps.prose: On a bottom-release rifle, a bolt release button that is jammed instead means the action went back cocked. Screws out, action out, cock it, dry fire it, and refit.
deepSteps.quote: Cycle the bolt several times to be sure that it functions properly. If you are unable to close the bolt handle completely, the action screws may be reversed.
deepSteps.cite: Models 10/110 (excluding ‘LE SERIES’), 11/111, 14/114 and 16/116 Bolt Action Centerfire Rifles — REV. 3 (08/19) — printed on the manual's own back page as "108831 REV. 3 (08/19)" — Section 3, Installing the Stock, p.9

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Bolt out, rifle horizontal, ejection port facing DOWN
Correct-calibre rod from the CHAMBER end and out the muzzle — never from the muzzle
Powder solvent on the brush, several passes; then clean patches until they come out clean
One oiled patch, then one dry patch to remove the excess
Check the bore afterwards for pieces of cleaning patch or any other obstruction

cleaning.name: BOLT ASSEMBLY (exterior only)
tasks: DO NOT DISASSEMBLE THE BOLT ASSEMBLY — Savage bars it outright
Wipe the body; work solvent around the bolt head, extractor and ejector
Inspect bolt head, extractor and ejector for damage or excessive wear while it is out
Verify the four digits by the extractor against the last four of the receiver serial number before refitting
Never fit a bolt from another rifle — they are serial-matched

cleaning.name: ACTION, STOCK & MAGAZINE
tasks: Soft cloth for mud, twigs and grass, then a thin coat of oil on cleaned metal
Clean and lightly oil interior metal surfaces where accessible, with the bolt out
With the stock removed, inspect the AccuTrigger and its adjustment spring for damage or debris
Leave the top-load magazine assembly in the stock; never pull on its feeding lips or sides
Do not tighten the small screw at the rear of the trigger guard — it will damage the stock

cleaning.name: MUZZLE BRAKE (only if fitted)
tasks: Adjustable brake: put it in the CLOSED position after each use
Use a cleaning solvent that contains NO oil, such as brake cleaner
Open and close the brake to work the solvent through and flush residue out
Never oil an adjustable brake — it increases carbon build-up and can cause a malfunction
Bolt open and no ammunition present before any brake work

reassembly: Confirm the chamber and magazine are empty and the bore is clear of patch material.
BOTTOM-RELEASE rifles: the bolt must still be closed and the action uncocked ('fired') before the action goes back into the stock.
Place the action into the stock, aligning the trigger with the trigger slot; leave the magazine out while reassembling.
Start both action screws — longer to the rear, shorter to the front — until the threads just engage the receiver; the stock stays loose at this stage.
Stand the rifle on its recoil pad with the barrel pointing upward and press down on the barrel to seat the recoil lug.
Tighten the front action screw first, then the rear action screw, securely. Do not tighten the small rear trigger-guard screw.

Fit the bolt: rotate the front baffle to line the bolt guide up with the extractor, hold the trigger fully rearward, press the bolt release (bottom) or the cocking indicator (side) down, and slide the bolt in with no ammunition present.
If the bolt release button is jammed after installing the action, take the screws and action out, lift and close the bolt handle to cock it, dry fire with the muzzle safe, and refit.
When reinserting a detachable box magazine, put the rear in first and pivot the front upward until it snaps into place.
fncheck: Cycle the bolt several times and confirm it closes fully; if the bolt handle will not close completely, the action screws are reversed and must be swapped. Verify the three position safety works in all three positions as described in Section 2 — FULL SAFE with the trigger blocked and the bolt locked closed, MID SAFE with the bolt free but the trigger still blocked, and OFF with the red dot exposed. With the bolt handle fully upward, the bolt to the rear, the muzzle safe and the safety at MID SAFE, the trigger should have no rearward movement. On a top-load rifle, reach into the receiver and press down on the plastic magazine follower to confirm it moves freely; if it binds, the stock comes off and the magazine assembly's position gets rechecked. Look through the bore against a light for obstructions including pieces of patch, and check the action screws are secure — Savage calls checking them before and after each shooting session good practice.
